objectives.summary: Before rolling out Microsoft Copilot and agents, you need to find SharePoint and OneDrive content that is shared too broadly, because Copilot surfaces anything a user can already reach. SharePoint Advanced Management (SAM) provides data access governance (DAG) reports, AI insights, site access reviews, restricted access control (RAC) and Restricted Content Discovery (RCD). Together they let you identify oversharing and either reduce discoverability or tighten access.

keyFacts.fact: Data access governance reports are found in the SharePoint admin center under Reports > Data access governance and help identify sites with potentially overshared or sensitive content. Snapshot reports and activity reports (for example sharing links created in the last 28 days) are available.

DAG report types include permission state reports for sites/OneDrive/files, site permissions for a given user, sensitivity label snapshot, sharing links activity, and Everyone except external users (EEEU) insights; reports can also be generated with SharePoint Online PowerShell (Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight).

Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting that stops a site's content from appearing in organization-wide search and Copilot responses; it does not change permissions and users with access can still open content directly. It applies to SharePoint sites only, not OneDrive.

RCD can be enabled in the SharePoint admin center (Active sites > site > Settings) or with Set-SPOSite -Identity <url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true. Index propagation can take a long time; sites with more than 500,000 items can take over a week.

Remediation options after a DAG report include restricted access control (limit a site to a specific group), reviewing the Change history report, and initiating a site access review so site owners update permissions.

objectives.portalPath: SharePoint admin center > Reports > Data access governance; SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > (site) > Settings > Restrict content discovery

lab.title: Find overshared sites and hide one from Copilot
steps: Sign in to the SharePoint admin center as a SharePoint Administrator in a tenant licensed for Microsoft Copilot with SharePoint Advanced Management available (both are needed for Restricted Content Discovery).
Go to Reports > Data access governance and, under the sharing links or EEEU category, select View reports and run a report.
Review the sites with the most Anyone or organization-wide links and pick a test site (for example 'Contoso HR Test').
Go to Sites > Active sites, select the test site, open the Settings tab and turn Restrict content discovery (Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot) On, then Save.
Optionally run in SharePoint Online PowerShell: Get-SPOSite -Identity https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/hrtest | Select RestrictContentOrgWideSearch
lab.verify: The site shows a Restricted tag and the PowerShell property RestrictContentOrgWideSearch returns True; after index propagation the site's files stop appearing in org-wide search results.

questions.scenario: Contoso is piloting Microsoft 365 Copilot. The Finance site must stay accessible to its current members, but its content must not appear in Copilot responses or organization-wide search while permissions are reviewed.
questions.question: What should you configure on the Finance site?

questions.explanation: RCD hides a site's content from org-wide search and Copilot without changing permissions, which matches the requirement. Removing EEEU and breaking inheritance changes permissions and could remove legitimate access, which the scenario forbids during review.

objectives.summary: Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) for AI gives a central place to see AI activity, sensitive data in prompts and responses, and oversharing risk for Copilot, agents and third-party AI apps. A classic DSPM for AI experience still exists, while a newer unified Data Security Posture Management adds objectives, AI observability and Security Copilot agents. Key tools are one-click policies, data risk assessments, Activity explorer and recommendations.

keyFacts.fact: DSPM for AI automatically runs a weekly default data risk assessment for the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage; custom data risk assessments (preview) can target specific users or sites.
DSPM for AI offers one-click preconfigured policies; allow at least 24 hours for new policies to collect data. Using it requires permissions such as the Microsoft Entra Compliance Administrator role.

From a data risk assessment's Protect tab you can restrict access by label (DLP policy that stops Copilot summarizing labeled data), restrict all items with SharePoint Restricted Content Discovery, create an auto-labeling policy, or create retention policies.
Activity explorer shows AI interactions (prompts and responses), sensitive information types and AI website visits, grouped into Copilot experiences and agents, Enterprise AI apps, and Other AI apps.

The newer Data Security Posture Management adds data security objectives (such as preventing data exposure in Copilot interactions) and AI observability, an inventory of AI apps and agents with activity in the last 30 days.

steps: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal as a Compliance Administrator.
Go to Solutions > DSPM for AI (classic) > Overview and confirm Microsoft Purview Audit is turned on.
In Recommendations, activate a one-click policy such as 'Detect risky interactions in AI apps' or the policy to extend insights for data discovery.
Open Data risk assessments > Microsoft 365 tab and select View details on the default assessment.
Select a site and review the Identify, Protect and Monitor tabs; note the Restrict all items (Restricted Content Discovery) option.
lab.verify: The policies appear on the Policies page, and after 24 hours Reports and Activity explorer begin showing AI interaction data. The default assessment lists sites with sensitive items and Anyone links.

objectives.summary: Copilot Studio custom agents can call an external threat detection system at runtime before each tool invocation, and Microsoft Defender can act as that system. When real-time protection is enabled, Defender scans tool invocations, blocks suspicious actions such as cross-prompt injection, and raises alerts. Setup is a joint task between a Security Administrator in the Defender portal and a Power Platform administrator. The Copilot Studio side of the feature is documented as preview.

keyFacts.fact: In the Defender portal go to Settings > Security for AI > Get started, select the Copilot Studio step and toggle Real-time protection on; then share the provided URL with the Power Platform administrator and paste back the Entra App ID.

The Power Platform administrator configures it in Power Platform admin center > Security > Threat detection > Additional threat detection, selecting the environment, allowing data sharing, entering the Entra App ID and the endpoint link (preview).
If the threat detection system does not answer within one second, the agent allows the tool call by default; Set error behavior can be changed to Block the query.
External threat detection is only called for generative agents that use generative orchestration; classic agents are skipped.
If the Microsoft 365 connector is not connected, real-time protection still blocks suspicious Copilot Studio activity, but related alerts and incidents do not appear in the Defender portal.

Real-time protection uses a built-in Default rule that only audits, plus custom rules that block chosen detection types (secret exfiltration, malicious content propagation, evasion techniques, unsafe email domain) scoped to specific agents.

objectives.portalPath: Microsoft Defender portal > Settings > Security for AI > Get started > Copilot Studio; Power Platform admin center > Security > Threat detection > Additional threat detection

lab.title: Connect Copilot Studio real-time protection to Defender
steps: As a Security Administrator, open the Microsoft Defender portal and go to Settings > Security for AI > Get started.
Connect the Microsoft 365 connector with at least Microsoft Entra ID Management events and Microsoft 365 activities selected.
Select the Copilot Studio step, toggle Real-time protection on and copy the Power Platform integration URL.

As a Power Platform administrator, register the Microsoft Entra application described in the Copilot Studio article, then go to Power Platform admin center > Security > Threat detection > Additional threat detection, pick a test environment, select Allow Copilot Studio to share data with a threat detection provider, enter the App ID and endpoint, and Save.
Paste the App ID into the Defender portal App ID field and select Save.
In Defender go to Settings > Security for AI > Policies & rules > Real-time protection and create a custom rule that blocks Secret exfiltration for a test agent.
lab.verify: The Copilot Studio step shows Connected on the Get started page and the custom rule is listed as enabled on the Real-time protection page.

objectives.summary: Conditional Access for agents extends the Conditional Access engine to Microsoft Entra Agent ID. You must target the right token subject: a user (on-behalf-of access), an agent identity or blueprint (app-only access), or an agent's user account. Policies can use agent risk from ID Protection (preview) and custom security attributes to scale. Agents can't satisfy interactive controls like MFA, so they need their own policies. Microsoft Entra Agent ID itself is documented as preview, and the agent user targeting options are labelled preview.

keyFacts.fact: Conditional Access for agents requires Microsoft 365 E7, or a Microsoft Agent 365 license paired with at least Microsoft Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3; creating policies needs the Conditional Access Administrator role.

Access patterns map to policy targets: on-behalf-of (delegated) targets users and groups; app-only targets an agent identity or agent identity blueprint; agent-user access targets the agent's user account. A policy for one subject doesn't apply to the others.
Policies scoped through the Users assignment, including All users, don't apply to agent user accounts; you must select Agents and then All agent users (preview) or specific agent users.

Targeting an agent identity blueprint covers every agent identity created from it, including future ones; custom security attributes let policies apply automatically to agents with matching attributes.

To block risky agents, include All agent identities, target All resources, set Conditions > Agent risk (preview) to High, grant Block, and start in Report-only mode. Agent risk-based policies additionally need Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft 365 E5 alongside Agent 365 (E7 covers both).
Conditional Access doesn't apply when an agent uses an API key instead of Entra tokens, or when security defaults are enabled.

objectives.portalPath: Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy > Users, agents or workload identities > Agents

lab.title: Create a report-only policy that blocks high-risk agent identities
steps: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as a Conditional Access Administrator in a tenant with the required Agent 365 licensing.
Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies and select New policy; name it 'CA-Agents-BlockHighRisk'.
Under Assignments select Users, agents or workload identities, choose Agents, and include All agent identities.
Under Target resources include All resources.
Under Conditions > Agent risk (Preview) set Configure to Yes and select High.
Under Grant select Block, set Enable policy to Report-only, and select Create.
lab.verify: The policy is listed in Report-only state; sign-in logs for agent identities show the report-only result for the policy.

AgentC acts as a digital worker with its own account, so target the agent's user account. A policy on one subject doesn't cover the others, so the alternative choices would leave each agent unprotected.

objectives.summary: Microsoft Defender XDR gives an AI agent inventory with risk levels and attack-surface relationships, and its incident graph includes blast radius analysis that shows possible paths from a compromised entity to critical targets. For agents managed through Microsoft Agent 365, Defender correlates agent alerts into incidents so analysts can trace root cause and blast radius. These agent detection capabilities and the blast radius graph are documented as preview, and Learn does not document a separate 'agent-only' blast radius tool beyond these experiences.

keyFacts.fact: Detection and investigation of threats to AI agents in Microsoft Defender is in public preview and covers agents managed through Microsoft Agent 365; analysts use the incident graph to see relationships between entities and the blast radius of AI agent threats.

Blast radius analysis in the incident graph (preview, in the legacy incident experience) is built on the Microsoft Sentinel data lake and graph, shows possible propagation paths from a selected node to predefined critical targets, and requires Sentinel data lake onboarding; Learn states it's available to customers who onboarded to the data lake before September 23, 2026.

In the incident graph, select a node and choose View blast radius; the view shows the top-rated attack paths, and path calculations are bounded to up to seven hops. Exposure management (read) permission or higher is needed.
Blast radius accuracy depends on available environment data; if critical assets aren't defined, the graph won't fully represent risk.

Assets > AI agents in the Defender portal shows each agent's risk level, risk indicators, recommendations, alerts, identity information and attack-surface relationships; the AgentsInfo Advanced Hunting table holds agent inventory data.

objectives.portalPath: Microsoft Defender portal > Incidents > (incident) > Attack story > select node > View blast radius; Assets > AI agents

lab.title: Review agent posture and query agent inventory
steps: Sign in to the Microsoft Defender portal with security reader access in a tenant onboarded to Agent 365 security.
Go to Assets > AI agents > Agents and filter by Risk level = High.
Open an agent page and review Risk indicators, Identity and authentication, and attack-surface relationships on the Overview tab.
Go to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting and run: AgentsInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId | where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
If an incident involving an agent exists, open its attack story, select the agent or related identity node, and choose View blast radius.
lab.verify: The query returns one current row per agent; the blast radius view displays paths from the node to critical targets (or 'No blast radius found').

objectives.summary: Managing Entra Agent ID access means assigning accountable humans (owners and sponsors), granting least-privilege access through entitlement management access packages, and disabling agents or blueprints when needed. Owners are technical administrators; sponsors are accountable for lifecycle and access. Admins can disable individual agents, entire blueprints, or block agent authentication tenant-wide with Conditional Access. Microsoft Entra Agent ID is documented as preview.

keyFacts.fact: Sponsors are required when creating agent identities and blueprints; agent identity sponsors can be users or select groups (dynamic or Microsoft 365) with up to 100 sponsors, no more than 5 groups. They can disable or delete the agent and modify its sponsors.

Owners are optional, can be users or service principals (not groups), can edit authentication properties and credentials, and unlike sponsors can re-enable a disabled agent identity, restore soft-deleted identities, or hard-delete them.
Owners and sponsors manage their agents in the My Account portal (Manage agents) and request access packages for them in the My Access portal ('Requesting for Sponsored agent' or 'Owned agent').
If a sponsor leaves the organization, sponsorship automatically transfers to the sponsor's manager; Lifecycle Workflows provide mover and leaver tasks to notify managers and cosponsors.

Disable scopes: individual agent (admin center or My Account), blueprint level (blocks existing agent identities and creation of new ones), or tenant-wide with Conditional Access policies that block agent authentication. Agent ID Administrator can disable agents in Entra ID > Agents.
Access packages for agents can grant security group memberships, application OAuth API permissions (including Microsoft Graph application permissions) and Microsoft Entra roles.

objectives.portalPath: Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities / Agent blueprints; My Account > Manage agents; My Access > Access packages

lab.title: Disable and re-enable a test agent identity
steps: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as an Agent ID Administrator.
Browse to Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities and select a test agent such as 'Contoso Budget Agent'.
Review its owners and sponsors, then select Disable.
As the agent's sponsor, sign in to https://myaccount.microsoft.com, open Manage agents, and confirm the agent shows as disabled; note that a sponsor can't re-enable it.
As an owner or admin, select the agent and choose Enable agent.
lab.verify: While disabled, the agent can't be issued tokens; after an owner re-enables it, token issuance resumes and audit logs record both actions.

Blocking All agent identities is tenant-wide and would affect unrelated agents. Removing sponsors doesn't stop authentication and sponsors are required. Blocking in the Microsoft 365 admin center affects availability in Microsoft 365 apps, not Entra token issuance.

objectives.summary: The AI gateway in Azure API Management governs traffic to language model APIs, MCP servers and agents. Key policies are llm-token-limit for TPM limits and quotas, semantic caching backed by Azure Managed Redis, and content safety checks using Azure AI Content Safety. You can import a Microsoft Foundry API with these policies preconfigured, or enable AI Gateway directly from the Foundry portal (the Foundry integration is preview).

keyFacts.fact: The llm-token-limit policy enforces tokens-per-minute limits or token quotas over hourly to yearly periods on any counter key (for example subscription ID or IP) and can precalculate prompt tokens to reject oversized requests before they reach the backend.

Semantic caching uses llm-semantic-cache-store and llm-semantic-cache-lookup with Azure Managed Redis or another RediSearch-compatible external cache and an Embeddings API to reuse completions for similar prompts.
When importing a Microsoft Foundry API, the wizard offers tabs for Manage token consumption, Apply semantic caching, and AI content safety (llm-content-safety policy) to block unsafe prompts.

AI gateway in Microsoft Foundry (preview): in the Foundry portal, Manage > AI Gateway > Add AI Gateway either creates a Basic v2 APIM instance or reuses an existing v2-tier instance in the same tenant and subscription; new projects are enabled by default but existing projects must be added manually.
A request exceeding the TPM limit returns 429 Too Many Requests; exceeding the total token quota returns 403 Forbidden. Limits apply at project level.
AI gateway content safety can enable Prompt Shields for jailbreak and prompt-injection detection and blocklists, and can start in log-only mode before blocking (AI Gateway tier, preview).

objectives.portalPath: Foundry portal > Manage > AI Gateway > Add AI Gateway; Azure portal > API Management > APIs > Add API > Microsoft Foundry

In the Foundry portal (new Foundry toggle on) select Manage > AI Gateway > Add AI Gateway, pick the Foundry resource, choose Create new (Basic v2), name it and select Add.
Wait until status is Enabled, select the gateway, locate an existing project and select Add project to gateway.
Configure a low TPM token limit for the project's model deployment on the AI Gateway pane.
Send several rapid requests to the model through the project endpoint.
In the Azure portal open the APIM instance > Monitoring > Metrics > Requests to confirm traffic flows through the gateway.
lab.verify: Requests increment the APIM Requests metric and calls exceeding the TPM limit return HTTP 429.

objectives.summary: Defender for AI Services is a Defender for Cloud plan that provides runtime threat protection for Microsoft Foundry and Azure OpenAI workloads, working with Prompt Shields and Microsoft threat intelligence to alert on jailbreaks, data leakage and credential theft. You enable it per subscription on the Defender plans page and then choose components such as suspicious prompt evidence, data security for AI interactions (Purview, preview) and AI model security (preview). Alerts integrate with Defender XDR.

keyFacts.fact: Enable the plan in Azure portal > Defender for Cloud > Environment settings > subscription > Defender plans by toggling AI services On; Owner or Contributor level is needed.

Plan components include suspicious prompt evidence (GA), data security for AI interactions (preview; uses Microsoft Purview and is a paid Purview feature not included in the plan), and AI model security (preview) for models in Azure Machine Learning registries.
If user prompt evidence is disabled, Defender for Cloud still analyzes prompts and responses for threats but masks prompt content in alerts.

AI threat protection is generally available, includes a 30-day free trial capped at 75 billion tokens scanned, scans text tokens only, and isn't available for connected AWS accounts or Azure Government.
You can add end-user and application context parameters to Azure AI API calls so alerts identify the user or app behind a request.

objectives.portalPath: Azure portal > Microsoft Defender for Cloud > Environment settings > (subscription) > Defender plans > AI services > Settings

lab.title: Enable Defender for AI Services with prompt evidence
steps: Sign in to the Azure portal with Owner or Contributor on a trial subscription that contains an Azure OpenAI or Foundry resource.
Open Microsoft Defender for Cloud > Environment settings and select the subscription.
On Defender plans, toggle AI services to On.
Select Settings next to AI services and toggle Enable user prompt evidence to On, then select Continue and Save.
Optionally send a known jailbreak-style test prompt to the model from the Foundry playground.

objectives.summary: In Microsoft Foundry, a guardrail is a named collection of controls; each control defines a risk, the intervention points to scan and the action (annotate or annotate and block). Models support user input and output intervention points, while agents add tool call and tool response (preview). Prompt Shields detect user prompt attacks and document (indirect) attacks. Agent guardrails are in preview, and an agent's guardrail fully overrides its model's guardrail.

keyFacts.fact: Four intervention points exist: user input, tool call (preview, agents only), tool response (preview, agents only), and output.
Risks in an agent are detected based on the guardrail assigned to the agent, not its underlying model; the agentic guardrail fully overrides the model's guardrail.

Blocking levels for harm categories: Low blocks only high severity, Medium blocks medium and high, High blocks low, medium and high; turning output filtering off requires approval for modified guardrails.
User prompt attack detection is on by default; document attack detection is off by default and must be enabled. Document attacks can be scanned at the tool response point for agents (preview).

Microsoft Default guardrails such as Default.V2 can't be edited; create a custom guardrail. Violence, Hate, Sexual and Self-harm controls on inputs and outputs can only be overridden, not deleted. Creating guardrails needs Foundry Account Owner or higher.
A guardrail can also be specified per request with the x-policy-id header, which overrides the deployment-level configuration for that call.

objectives.portalPath: Foundry portal > (project) > Build > Guardrails > Create guardrail

lab.title: Create a custom guardrail with indirect attack protection for an agent
steps: With Foundry Account Owner on a test Foundry project that has a model deployment and an agent, open the Foundry portal and select Build > Guardrails > Create Guardrail.

Select the risk Document attack (indirect attack), choose the tool response intervention point, and action Annotate and block, then select Add control (Spotlighting isn't supported for agents, so leave it off).
Override the Violence control to the High blocking level on user input and output and confirm the override.
Select Next, Add agents, pick your test agent, and Save.
Name the guardrail 'Contoso-Agent-Guardrail' and select Create.
Select the guardrail row and choose Try in Playground to send test prompts.
lab.verify: When a blocking control triggers, the playground shows which risk was detected and at which intervention point; the agent lists the new guardrail under Guardrails.

questions.scenario: A Contoso agent uses a web search tool. Attackers hide instructions in web pages that the tool returns to the agent.
questions.question: Which control should you add to the agent's guardrail?
options: Document attack at the tool response intervention point with Annotate and block
User prompt attack at the output intervention point
Protected material text at the user input intervention point
Hate at the tool call intervention point set to Low
questions.explanation: Indirect prompt injection arrives in tool-returned content, so scanning the tool response for document attacks and blocking stops it before it enters agent memory. User prompt attacks only apply at user input, and output is the wrong point. Protected material detects copyrighted text, not injection. A Hate control on tool calls checks outbound content for hate speech, not injected instructions.

questions.scenario: After enabling a strict Prompt Shields control in the guardrail assigned to a model deployment, legitimate prompts from Fabrikam's help desk app are being blocked.
questions.question: What should you do first to investigate without disrupting users?
options: Change the control action from block to annotate
Delete the user prompt attack control from Default.V2
Assign the model to no guardrail
Raise the Violence blocking level to High
questions.explanation: Learn's troubleshooting advice for false positives is to switch from block to annotate mode so detections are logged without filtering. Default.V2 can't be edited. Models always fall back to the Microsoft Default rather than no guardrail. Changing the Violence level doesn't affect Prompt Shields sensitivity, which is configured separately. Note that the annotate-only action is available for models; agent guardrails support only Annotate and block.

objectives.summary: The Data and AI security dashboard in Defender for Cloud gives one view of data and AI resources, their protection coverage, top issues and internet exposure. It has overview, top issues, Data closer look and AI closer look sections, the last of which shows AI discovery, prompts scanned and AI alerts. Full functionality depends on Defender CSPM with sensitive data discovery, Defender for Storage, Defender for Databases and AI threat protection.

keyFacts.fact: Full access requires Defender CSPM with the sensitive data discovery extension, Defender for Storage, Defender for Databases and threat protection for AI workloads; each subscription must be registered to the Microsoft.Security resource provider.
The minimum RBAC role to use the dashboard is Security explorer, with permissions to read assessments, subassessments and alerts.
The AI closer look section shows AI discovery, AI threat protection (prompts scanned and alerts by severity), AI queries in security explorer, and internet-exposed resources used for grounding.
The Top issues section lists highest-severity alerts by MITRE ATT&CK tactic, critical and high recommendations, and critical and high attack paths.
The dashboard is a Defender CSPM feature that's GA in Azure commercial but not available in Azure Government.

objectives.summary: The Microsoft 365 admin center (Agents > All agents) is where admins inventory, deploy, pin, block and remove agents for Copilot and Microsoft 365 apps. The agent Registry lists agents with actions such as Install, Uninstall, Block, Update in store and Pin for users. With Microsoft Agent 365, admins also activate template agents and manage or block individual agent instances. Blocking scope differs by how the agent was built.

keyFacts.fact: Block or unblock agents for the whole organization in Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > select agent > Block or Unblock.

Blocking a Copilot Studio or Agent Builder agent affects its availability in Microsoft Copilot and other hosts such as Outlook and Teams, but blocking an agent created with SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only affects availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
Registry actions include Install, Uninstall, Block (also removes it from users who installed it), Update in store, and Pin for users; admins can add up to five tags per agent.
Inventory filters such as Availability > All users, Availability > No users, and Missing an owner help find agents to deploy, block or remove.
For Agent 365 agents, blocking an agent turns off all its instances until unblocked; individual instances can be blocked from the agent's Instances tab.

objectives.portalPath: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > Registry > (agent) > Block / Install / Pin for users
